depiction.primary_object: three stacked rows of circular bullet points and horizontal lines

readings.meaning: list view or menu UI toggle

ambiguity: Within a task manager, a generic list icon is meta-chrome and visually indistinct from a hamburger menu or text alignment icon; almost any real-world list has a concrete topic (groceries, packing, guests) that deserves its own specific icon.
task_intents: compile a master checklist or inventory
make a pros and cons list
brainstorm a wish list of items

Make a shortlist of five contractors to call for quotes
Put together a shared reading list for the summer seminar
Consolidate three scattered to-do lists into one weekly backlog
Write up bullet-point talking points for tomorrow's board update
Check off completed items and archive
Write out a step-by-step closing checklist for the evening shift staff to follow
Make an itemized list of everything stored in the attic boxes for insurance

near_misses.task: Write grocery list for Sunday dinner

near_misses.better: invoice or receipt with dollar sign

reasoning: The icon shows three bullet points with lines, the standard UI glyph for a bulleted list or list-view toggle. Inside a to-do list app it is redundant interface chrome, and even when a task is literally about making a list (groceries, packing, guests), the list's concrete subject is always a better icon.
